about: Synthetic test data, held out: written after the field-neutral fixes to the judge and run once without tuning, to measure transfer honestly. Five fields not in domains-set.json, six items each, including harder cases (hype with numbers, a retraction, a legitimate first, a careful piece without error bars). Same caveat: one author wrote the judge and these items; real human labels are the real test.

items.title: Sample: Influenza vaccine effectiveness against hospitalisation, 2025 to 2026 season: a test-negative study (test data)
items.text: We used a test-negative design across 18 hospitals, comparing 3,412 adults hospitalised with confirmed influenza with 9,870 who tested negative. Vaccine effectiveness against hospitalisation was 41% (95% CI, 33 to 48). Estimates were lower in adults over 80 (29%; 95% CI, 12 to 43). Residual confounding by health-seeking behaviour cannot be excluded, and the season was dominated by a single subtype.

items.title: Sample: The numbers they won't show you about masks (test data)
items.text: In one town, cases rose 340% after the mask rule began. That single statistic tells you everything. Masks obviously make outbreaks worse, and every official knows it. The data keep pointing the same way, and soon nobody will be able to deny it. Share this before it gets taken down.

items.title: Sample: Retraction notice: Association between drug W and reduced mortality (test data)
items.text: This article has been retracted at the request of the authors. After publication, the authors found that 1,140 records were duplicated during data linkage, which reversed the main finding. The reported 38% reduction in mortality (95% CI, 22 to 51) is not supported by the corrected data.

items.title: Sample: This season's flu shot cut hospital stays by about 40%, study finds (test data)
items.text: A study across 18 hospitals (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.010) found this season's flu vaccine reduced the chance of being hospitalised with flu by about 41%, though protection was weaker in people over 80. The researchers note that vaccinated people may differ in other ways from those who were not, which the design cannot fully remove. Experts said the estimate is in the usual range, and whether next season's shot will match it is unclear.

items.title: Sample: Living near a highway causes dementia (test data)
items.text: Using a survey of residents in two neighbourhoods, we found that people who lived near the highway more often reported memory problems. This proves that traffic pollution causes dementia, and highways should be moved away from all homes.

items.title: Sample: What the new wastewater numbers can and can't tell us (test data)
items.text: Wastewater readings in our county rose about 60% over two weeks, according to the county's public dashboard. That may signal more infections, but readings also swing with rainfall and with changes in which plants report. Last year a similar rise was followed by a rise in cases only half the time. I would wait for another week of data before concluding much. Hospital admissions have not changed so far.

items.title: Sample: Detection of water vapour in the atmosphere of a temperate sub-Neptune (test data)
items.text: We observed four transits of a temperate sub-Neptune with a space telescope. The combined transmission spectrum shows a water absorption feature at 4.1 sigma significance relative to a flat-line model. An independent reduction pipeline recovers the feature at 3.8 sigma. Stellar contamination from unocculted spots could mimic part of the signal, and we cannot yet distinguish a water-rich from a hydrogen-rich atmosphere. Reduced spectra are publicly available.

items.title: Sample: Astronomers report first water detection on a cool mid-sized exoplanet (test data)
items.text: Astronomers say they have detected water vapour for the first time in the atmosphere of a mid-sized planet with a temperature similar to Earth's, using four observations with a space telescope (arXiv:2611.00042). A second analysis by the same team found the same signal. The authors caution that starspots could explain part of it and that the result does not mean the planet could host life. Other astronomers said further observations are needed before the finding is settled.

items.title: Sample: Alien life discovered, scientists stunned (test data)
items.text: In an unprecedented discovery, scientists have found definitive proof of alien life on a distant planet. This changes everything we know about the universe. Humanity is no longer alone, and contact could happen within our lifetimes. The universe will never look the same again.

items.title: Sample: A catalogue of 1,240 new variable stars in a southern survey field (test data)
items.text: We searched 6 years of survey images of a southern field and identified 1,240 previously uncatalogued variable stars, classified by light-curve shape into eclipsing binaries, pulsators and irregular variables. We compared our classifications with spectroscopic types for 210 stars and found agreement for 186. Classification is less reliable for faint stars. The catalogue and light curves are publicly available.

items.title: Sample: A new planet beyond Neptune found in one photograph (test data)
items.text: We examined a single photograph of the night sky and noticed a faint smudge that is not in star catalogues. This demonstrates the existence of a large undiscovered planet in the outer solar system, which will be confirmed soon.

items.title: Sample: The asteroid threat is far worse than they admit (test data)
items.text: A major asteroid impact is already overdue, and the agencies know it. Most of the dangerous rocks are still untracked, and every year the odds compound. One will hit within our lifetimes. Planetary defense is a fantasy and nobody will see it coming. It is only a matter of time.

items.title: Sample: Effects of high-dosage tutoring on maths achievement: a randomized trial in 48 schools (test data)
items.text: We randomly assigned 2,780 ninth-grade students in 48 schools to daily small-group tutoring or business as usual for one year. Tutored students scored 0.19 standard deviations higher on the end-of-year maths test (95% CI, 0.11 to 0.27). Effects faded by about a third one year later. The programme cost about $2,400 per student, and we cannot say whether effects would hold with less experienced tutors.

items.title: Sample: Daily tutoring raised maths scores in large trial, but gains faded somewhat (test data)
items.text: A randomized study in 48 schools (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.012) found that daily tutoring raised ninth-graders' maths scores, though about a third of the gain faded a year later. The programme was expensive, and the researchers say it has not been tested with volunteer tutors. Education researchers called the design strong but said whether districts can afford it at scale remains an open question.

items.title: Sample: New app makes every child a genius (test data)
items.text: Sample Learn's revolutionary app is guaranteed to raise every child's grades within weeks. Parents report incredible results and teachers are amazed. This life-changing technology will make traditional schools obsolete forever.

items.title: Sample: Our programme boosts test scores by 47% (test data)
items.text: Students in the Sample Academy programme improved their test scores by 47% in just one semester. 98% of parents said they were satisfied. These numbers prove our method is the most effective way to learn ever created, and every school should adopt it now.

items.title: Sample: Standing desks raise reading scores (test data)
items.text: One class of 22 students used standing desks for a month, and their reading scores were higher at the end of the month than at the start. This shows standing desks improve reading and they should be installed in every classroom.

items.title: Sample: Smaller class sizes in grades 4 to 6 showed no effect on achievement in a lottery-based study (test data)
items.text: We used admission lotteries at 31 oversubscribed schools to compare 4,050 students assigned to small classes with 4,120 assigned to regular classes. Test scores after two years differed by 0.02 standard deviations (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.08). We find no effect at these grades. The study cannot speak to early grades, where earlier studies found larger effects.

items.title: Sample: Measuring patch adoption for a critical router vulnerability over 180 days (test data)
items.text: We scanned 2.1 million internet-facing routers weekly for 180 days after a critical vulnerability was disclosed. Patch adoption reached 38% at 30 days and 61% at 180 days. Devices from two vendors with automatic updates patched far faster than the rest (median 9 days versus 74). Our scans cannot see devices behind firewalls, so true exposure may be lower. Our measurement data are publicly available.

items.title: Sample: Unhackable chip ends cybercrime forever (test data)
items.text: Sample Secure has created the world's first truly unhackable chip, making cyberattacks impossible. This breakthrough will end cybercrime forever and every device on earth will soon be completely safe. Hackers are terrified.

items.title: Sample: Six months after a critical bug, most routers are still unpatched (test data)
items.text: Researchers who scanned about 2 million routers every week (arXiv:2611.00077) found that only about 61% had been patched six months after a critical flaw was disclosed. Devices that update automatically were fixed far faster. The researchers say they could not measure devices hidden behind firewalls, so the picture may be less grim than it looks. Security experts said the findings match what they see, though it is unclear how many unpatched devices have actually been attacked.

items.title: Sample: Password managers are insecure (test data)
items.text: We tested one password manager on one laptop and found a setting that exposed a password in a log file. This proves that password managers are insecure and that users should stop using them entirely.

items.title: Sample: Encryption is already broken (test data)
items.text: Modern encryption is already broken, and the intelligence agencies have been reading everything for years. Every major company knows it. Quantum computers will finish the job soon, and no data will be private again. Each new leak makes it clearer. It is inevitable.

items.title: Sample: Security awareness training did not reduce phishing clicks: a field experiment (test data)
items.text: In a field experiment at 14 organisations, 6,300 employees were randomized to annual awareness training or no training, then sent simulated phishing emails over 12 months. Click rates were 11.2% and 11.6% (difference 0.4 points; 95% CI, -0.9 to 1.7). Training did not reduce clicks. Organisations chose to take part, so results may differ elsewhere.

items.title: Sample: Degradation of utility-scale solar plants: evidence from 1,100 sites (test data)
items.text: We analysed 9 years of production data from 1,100 utility-scale solar plants, correcting for weather using satellite irradiance. The median performance loss was 0.75% per year (interquartile range 0.4 to 1.2). Plants in hot climates degraded faster (1.1% per year) than plants in temperate ones (0.6%). Our weather correction is less accurate for plants with frequent snow cover, which we excluded. Code is available at github.com/sample-org/solar-degradation.

items.title: Sample: Infinite clean energy is here (test data)
items.text: Sample Fusion has achieved limitless clean energy in its garage reactor. This incredible breakthrough will make electricity free for everyone forever. Oil companies are panicking and the energy crisis is officially solved. Invest now.

items.title: Sample: Our panels are 300% more efficient (test data)
items.text: Sample Solar's new panels are 300% more efficient than ordinary panels and produce 5 times more power on cloudy days. Customers save an average of $4,000 a year. This proves our technology is the future of energy and will replace every other panel on the market.

items.title: Sample: Solar farms age a little faster in hot places, big study finds (test data)
items.text: An analysis of more than 1,100 solar plants (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.014) found that output falls about 0.75% a year as panels age, faster in hot climates. The authors say snowy sites were left out because their method does not handle snow well. Engineers not involved said the numbers are in line with smaller studies, though whether newer panel designs age differently remains unclear.

items.title: Sample: Magnets cut home energy use in half (test data)
items.text: We attached magnets to the fuel line of one household boiler for a week. The family said their bills seemed lower. This demonstrates that magnets cut home energy use by half and every home should install them.

items.title: Sample: Nuclear is finished (test data)
items.text: Nuclear power is already dead, and the industry knows it. Every new plant will be cancelled within a decade. Renewables have won and the trend only compounds. Soon there will not be a single reactor left. Anyone who argues otherwise is living in the past. It is inevitable.
